sense: a way of dealing with something

evidence: Quint. 6 pr. 14: aliqua vīvendī ratiō quaerenda est
Cic. Brut. 253: dē ratiōne Latīnē loquendī
terms.comment: Often with a gerund in the genitive: the way of doing something.
aliā viā aggredī, to try a different approach.

evidence: Cic. Att. 12.33: Damasippum velim aggrediāre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To go at a task, or to a person with a request; also, to attack.

phrases.latin: Dēceptus sum, at nōn dēfatīgātus. … Hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā.
phrases.english: I’ve been foiled, but I’m not worn out. … That way didn’t work; we’ll try another approach.

phrases.latin: sed vīvimus, et aliqua vīvendī ratiō quaerenda est
phrases.english: but we are alive, and some way of living must be found

sources: Lewis & Short: ratio · Lewis & Short: via · Lewis & Short: aggredior
